_transcription: PAGE MAP — 12 rendered pages (idx 0..11 = printed folios 1..12), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB5/5, SET No. 1, Q.P. Code 56/5/1, 'CHEMISTRY (Theory)', Time 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (folios 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK — a rule at the top, the footer '56/5/1  12', nothing else; CONFIRMED AT FULL SIZE, not read off the contact sheet, and unlike 2022 65/5/3 there is no show-through ghost on it. The alternating hypothesis HELD exactly: I montaged the top ~22% of all five odd indices and every one opens in HINDI (idx 1 'सामान्य निर्देश', idx 3 'खण्ड ख' + Q4 with its Hindi graph, idx 5 Q9(क), idx 7 'खण्ड ग' + the Q12 passage, idx 9 the Hindi Q12 (a)-(d)), so there is NO English overflow onto any odd top and no mid-paper parity inversion. English content runs continuously Q1 -> Q12: idx 2 = English General Instructions + SECTION A + Q1-Q3; idx 4 = SECTION B + Q4-Q8; idx 6 = Q9-Q11; idx 8 = SECTION C + Q12 lead-in, passage and cell diagram; idx 10 = Q12 sub-parts (a)-(d) and the (d) OR branch. Q12 is the only question split across a page boundary. ⚠ COVER vs FOLIO COUNT: the cover says 'contains 11 printed pages' while the booklet has 12 folios — the 12th is the blank one, so the cover is counting printed pages and is consistent; noted so nobody reads it as a missing page. STRUCTURE — read off the paper's own printed English General Instructions (idx 2) and it matches `term2_sci` EXACTLY, no disagreement: (1) 12 questions, all compulsory; (2) three sections A, B, C; (3) Section A = Q1-3, very short answer, 2 marks each; (4) Section B = Q4-11, short answer, 3 marks each; (5) Section C = Q12, case based, 5 marks; (6) log tables and calculators not allowed. 6 + 24 + 5 = 35, matching the cover's Maximum Marks 35 and the marking scheme's 'A full scale of marks 0-35 has to be used'. NO MCQs at all, so every row is `subjective`, no row carries an `answer` and there is no Section-A key table in the scheme. ⚠ INTERNAL CHOICE — CONFIRMING THE DISPATCH: this paper prints only SIX general instructions and NOT ONE of them mentions internal choice or gives a count, so the paper announces nothing and the marking scheme is the only authority. I walked the scheme question by question (ms/p02..p05): it reprints an explicit OR block under Q5, Q6, Q9, Q11 and under sub-part Q12(d), and under NO other question. That is FIVE internal choices, all ingested as paired rows with `_alternativeTo`. Q7 prints (a) and (b) with '2+1=3' and NO 'OR' — the scheme confirms it by giving both parts under one '7.' row — so Q7 is ONE question with two sub-parts, not a choice; same for Q1 ('Do any two' of three sub-parts, scheme marks it '1x2 (Any two)'), Q2, Q3 and Q8. Note the choices sit on DIFFERENT question numbers from the two sibling sets already transcribed (56/1/1 chose Q5/Q7/Q8/Q10/Q12(d), 56/2/1 chose Q4/Q6/Q8/Q10/Q12(iv)) — five each, but a count carried over from a sibling would have landed on the wrong questions. ⚠ DECIMAL POINTS — CONFIRMING THE DISPATCH: this QUESTION PAPER prints ORDINARY BASELINE full stops ('1.5 M', '138.9 S'), verified at zoom, so NO `{\cdot}` is used anywhere here. Its MARKING SCHEME does print raised dots ('0·693', '138·9', '0·208'), exactly the split the dispatch described — but the scheme is not transcribed, so nothing in this file is affected. CBSE-VOIDED QUESTIONS: NONE. I read all six marking-scheme pages including both pages of spot-evaluation instructions; there is no 'Full mark to be awarded for any option', no 'Award full mark if attempted (Printing error)' and no equivalent note anywhere in the document. The only marking accommodations are ordinary ones ('or any other suitable equation', 'Any two consequences', 'Any one difference', 'Deduct 1/2 mark for incorrect unit'). CHAPTERS: Q6, BOTH branches, is Surface Chemistry — (a) coagulation / Hardy-Schulze rule / electrophoresis is colloid chemistry and (b) physisorption vs chemisorption is adsorption — dropped from Class 12 at NCERT's rationalisation, so both rows are filed on `Surface Chemistry [Outdated]` and NOT on a plausible-looking neighbour. It is Q6 here, against Q10 on 56/1/1 and Q8 on 56/2/1, so the position genuinely moves between sets. Subtopics `Colloids` and `Adsorption` are the old NCERT Surface Chemistry chapter's own section headings and are the SAME TWO NAMES the other two 2022 agents chose independently; this paper needs no third. Every other question maps to one of the ten live chapters and nothing is out of syllabus, so no `_outOfSyllabus` flag was raised. 20 rows for 12 questions (12 primaries + 5 OR-alternatives + 3 extra case-study sub-parts). FIGURES: four rows carry `_figure`, all REQUIRED — Q4's rate-law graph (idx 4), Q11(a)'s drawn compound (idx 6, described WITHOUT naming it because the question asks for its IUPAC name) and Q12(a)/Q12(b), which depend on the drawn galvanic cell (idx 8) for referents the passage never supplies. questions._figure: REQUIRED — 'silver plate' appears NOWHERE in the passage; it is a label on the drawn cell, so without the figure the stem names a referent the reader has never met. The drawing shows two beakers, I on the left with a zinc plate in a \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)}\) solution and II on the right with a silver plate in \(\mathrm{Ag^{+}(aq)}\), joined by a salt bridge and by an external wire through a voltmeter. Page idx 8.
questions.context:
Oxidation-reduction reactions are commonly known as redox reactions. They involve transfer of electrons from one species to another. In a spontaneous reaction, energy is released which can be used to do useful work. The reaction is split into two half reactions. Two different containers are used and a wire is used to drive the electrons from one side to the other and a Voltaic/Galvanic cell is created. It is an electrochemical cell that uses spontaneous redox reactions to generate electricity. A salt bridge also connects to the half cells. The reading of the voltmeter gives the cell voltage or cell potential or electromotive force. If \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{cell}}\) is positive the reaction is spontaneous and if it is negative the reaction is non-spontaneous and is referred to as electrolytic cell. Electrolysis refers to the decomposition of a substance by an electric current. One mole of electric charge when passed through a cell will discharge half a mole of a divalent metal ion such as \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\). This was first formulated by Faraday in the form of laws of electrolysis.
The conductance of material is the property of materials due to which a material allows the flow of ions through itself and thus conducts electricity. Conductivity is represented by k and it depends upon nature and concentration of electrolyte, temperature etc. A more common term molar conductivity of a solution at a given concentration is conductance of the volume of solution containing one mole of electrolyte kept between two electrodes with the unit area of cross-section and distance of unit length. Limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolytes cannot be obtained graphically.
questions.stem: Is silver plate the anode or cathode?
